# ui-popout

Popouts: one item of a session or task in a small window of its own.

- **Runs in:** the UI (your Emacs)
- **Source:** [lisp/ui/harness-ui-popout.el](../../lisp/ui/harness-ui-popout.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [ui](ui.md), [ui-compose](ui-compose.md)
- **Required by:** [ui-quick-search](ui-quick-search.md), [ui-report](ui-report.md)

## About

A popout shows one thing a session or a task holds -- the request a
blocked session waits on, the report a task handed in -- in a small
window of its own, so it can be read and acted on without opening the
session or leaving the view it was opened from.  Whoever owns the item
draws it; this file gives every popout the same frame:

  header line   the title and a [close] button
  content       what the owner's RENDER function inserts, buttons,
                images and text-property keymaps included
  compose box   optional: the shared box, for a typed answer or feedback

The window is a side window at the bottom of the frame
(`harness-ui-popout-window-parameters`), selected, and fitted to its
content up to `harness-ui-popout-max-height`, or the popout's own
:max-height (a report with images grows taller).  Content taller
than that scrolls; while point is in the box, the box stays on the
window's last line, as a chat's does.  An image is not
drawn with the content: decoding one takes long enough that the
popout would open frozen, so a line where it goes says it is loading
and the image comes a moment later, growing the window
(`harness-ui-image-load`).  Each item has one popout, named by a
KEY the owner picks, such as (pending SESSION-ID) or (report
TASK-ID): showing the KEY again reuses its buffer, so state the
owner keeps buffer-locally there survives.  The owner calls
`harness-ui-popout-refresh` when the item changes and
`harness-ui-popout-close` once there is nothing left to show.

A popout can be opened from another, its :parent: an image of a
report, shown larger.  It takes the parent's window, its header says
[back], and closing it shows the parent there again, where it was.
`harness-ui-popout-image` is that image popout: one image as large as
the frame allows, which Emacs's image keys zoom.

On the content, `q` closes the popout and `g` draws it again; in the
box, the keys are the box's, and C-c C-c sends it.  The content is a
panel of the box (`harness-compose-panel-key`), as the panels of a
request it draws are: C-c . and a key presses that key on it from the
box, where q and g type.  C-g closes the popout once it has nothing
else to quit.  Text typed in the box of a popout that closes is kept
for the next time its KEY shows.

Views offer one key to pop out the item at point (`harness-ui-popout-at-point`,
SPC on the task board): the functions on
`harness-ui-popout-at-point-functions` each know one kind of item.

## Provides

### Hooks

- `harness-ui-popout-at-point-functions` — Functions popping out the item at point of a harness view.

### Commands

- `harness-ui-popout-at-point` — Pop out the item at point: what its session waits on, its report.
- `harness-ui-popout-quit` — Close this popout.
- `harness-ui-popout-redraw` — Draw this popout again.
- `harness-ui-popout-submit` — Send what this popout's box holds to the popout's owner.

### Options

- `harness-ui-popout-image-max-height` — Height an image popout grows to at most, as a fraction of its frame's.
- `harness-ui-popout-image-max-scale` — How many times larger than elsewhere an image popout shows an image at most.
- `harness-ui-popout-max-height` — Height a popout grows to at most, as a fraction of its frame's.
- `harness-ui-popout-min-height` — Height in lines of a popout with little content.
- `harness-ui-popout-window-parameters` — Where popouts appear: `display-buffer-in-side-window` parameters.

## Uses

### Hooks it adds to

- `harness-ui-redraw-hook` → `harness-ui-popout--refresh-all`
- `kill-buffer-hook` → `harness-ui-popout--on-kill`
- `pre-redisplay-functions` → `harness-ui-popout--follow`
